verdict.rationale: gstack runs as a skill pack inside AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, so users drive it conversationally. A top-level router skill "sends any gstack request to the right skill" (docs-18), skills declare speech-to-text natural-language aliases like "test the app" and "run QA" (docs-51), and /spec-style skills turn "vague intent" into executable specs (docs-21). Community reports describe conversational use via Claude in conductor.build (comm-1). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how free-form requests map to skills beyond the router one-liner, much of the surface is slash-command based, and no independent hands-on confirmation of natural-language routing accuracy.
